newsitem.title: FRANCE: Majority of French for Communist ministers--poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of French for Communist ministers--poll.

text.p: More French people favour inclusion of Communist ministers in the next government than oppose it, according to a poll carried out after projections of a left-wing victory in Sunday's election runoff.
The Sofres institute polled 1,000 people by telephone after voting closed at 1800 GMT and found 49 percent were in favour of Communist ministers and 46 percent opposed.

It was not clear when the poll result was published, at around 2100 GMT, whether the Socialist Party would obtain an absolute majority of 289 seats in the National Assembly, or fall short and need to depend on the Communist Party.

The poll, broadcast on TF1 television, also showed that 61 percent thought Conservative President Jacques Chirac should stay on and "cohabit" with a leftist government while 31 percent thought he should quit.
Asked who should be the real head of government, 58 percent responded that it should be the prime minister, while 37 percent said it should be the president.
Forty-eight percent thought the prospect of co-habitation between a left-wing government and a right-wing president was positive, while 45 percent saw it as negative.
Sixty percent doubted that such a co-habitation could last the full five-year term of the incoming legislature, while 35 percent thought it would not.
